Layout title objects

Source: R/zz-gen-layout.R
go_layout_title.Rd

The object for the figure layout's title. go_layout_title() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_layout_title(
  ...,
  automargin = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  pad = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  text = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  xanchor = NULL,
  xref = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  yanchor = NULL,
  yref = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

automargin

Determines whether the title can automatically push the figure margins. If `yref='paper'` then the margin will expand to ensure that the title doesn't overlap with the edges of the container. If `yref='container'` then the margins will ensure that the title doesn't overlap with the plot area, tick labels, and axis titles. If `automargin=true` and the margins need to be expanded, then y will be set to a default 1 and yanchor will be set to an appropriate default to ensure that minimal margin space is needed. Note that when `yref='paper'`, only 1 or 0 are allowed y values. Invalid values will be reset to the default 1. Logical.

font

Sets the title font. A go_font() object or named list, with properties color, family, lineposition, shadow, size, style, textcase, variant and weight (see go_font()).

pad

Sets the padding of the title. Each padding value only applies when the corresponding `xanchor`/`yanchor` value is set accordingly. E.g. for left padding to take effect, `xanchor` must be set to "left". The same rule applies if `xanchor`/`yanchor` is determined automatically. Padding is muted if the respective anchor value is "middle"/"center". A go_title_pad() object or named list, with properties b, l, r and t (see go_title_pad()).

subtitle

A go_title_subtitle() object or named list, with properties font and text (see go_title_subtitle()).

text

Sets the plot's title. String.

x

Sets the x position with respect to `xref` in normalized coordinates from 0 (left) to 1 (right). Number in the interval [0, 1].

xanchor

Sets the title's horizontal alignment with respect to its x position. "left" means that the title starts at x, "right" means that the title ends at x and "center" means that the title's center is at x. "auto" divides `xref` by three and calculates the `xanchor` value automatically based on the value of `x`. One of "auto", "left", "center", "right".

xref

Sets the container `x` refers to. "container" spans the entire `width` of the plot. "paper" refers to the width of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

y

Sets the y position with respect to `yref` in normalized coordinates from 0 (bottom) to 1 (top). "auto" places the baseline of the title onto the vertical center of the top margin. Number in the interval [0, 1].

yanchor

Sets the title's vertical alignment with respect to its y position. "top" means that the title's cap line is at y, "bottom" means that the title's baseline is at y and "middle" means that the title's midline is at y. "auto" divides `yref` by three and calculates the `yanchor` value automatically based on the value of `y`. One of "auto", "top", "middle", "bottom".

yref

Sets the container `y` refers to. "container" spans the entire `height` of the plot. "paper" refers to the height of the plotting area only. One of "container", "paper".

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_layout_title object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  update_layout(title = go_layout_title(text = "title"))
